name: Example: Identifying Whether a Vector Lies in the Null Space of a Given Matrix
problem:
The matrix $A$ and vectors $\mathbf{b}_1$, $\mathbf{b}_2$, $\mathbf{b}_3$ are given below. Which of the vectors lie in $\textrm{Null}(A)?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064430/assets/9832b17728be69381a5f534317c0f30156fd32f3706f4cd4634765a02370180e.png)
worked_solution:
A vector $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Null}(A)$ if $A\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{0}.$ So, we need to compute the product of $A$ and each of the given vectors and check whether it is equal to $\mathbf{0}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A{b}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -5 & 10 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-27 \\ 45 \\ 72\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -5 & 10 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0\,✓ \\ A{b}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -5 & 10 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 25 \\ 40\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only $\mathbf{b}_2$ lies in $\textrm{Null}(A).$
